1k3irmd: You found every part of a plant!
k1c4ze: Not yet! Find all 5 parts of the plant in Meet the Plant.
1o0sucb: Every plant has parts with special jobs. Tap each part of this plant to learn its job. Can you find all 5?
1pgocri: Roots grow under the ground. They hold the plant in place and slurp up water and minerals, like a bunch of straws!
1556et1: The stem holds the plant up tall. Tiny tubes inside carry water up to the leaves, like an elevator.
1juot8: Leaves are food factories! They use sunlight, air and water to make sugar for the plant. That is called photosynthesis.
1yiyiu7: The flower is where seeds get started. Bright petals invite bees, and the bees bring pollen.
1c91nm0: This pod is the plant's fruit! A fruit holds and protects the seeds. Every bean inside could grow a brand new plant.
1u3qsnr: Wiggle wiggle! Earthworms dig tunnels that let air and water reach the roots. Worms help plants grow!
2iq8xy: Butterflies sip sweet nectar from flowers. Pollen sticks to them and they carry it to the next flower!
102bf9i: The sun gives plants the energy they need to make their food.
55q8o0: Bonus: tap the wiggly worm, the butterfly and the sun.
1nkbmql: You dissected a bean seed and found the baby plant!
1vzd3j0: Not yet! Open the bean and find every part in Open a Seed.
1qlywke: Scientists open seeds to see what's inside, just like your class! First, tap the dry bean to soak it in water overnight.
j8141l: That skin is the seed coat. It's a tough jacket that protects the baby plant inside. Now drag the bean sideways to split it open!
1als969: These two big halves are cotyledons . They are stuffed with food, like a packed lunch for the baby plant.
bi52ce: You found the embryo. It's the baby plant! Look closer: it has a tiny root and tiny leaves. Tap them!
28g0q0: This pointy part is the baby root. When the seed sprouts, the root grows down first to find water.
1qpso98: These are the baby leaves. Folded up tight, they are waiting to grow up toward the sunlight.
p43vkp: You found every part! Press Watch it sprout to see what the embryo does next.
19nnikz: Into the water it goes! Soaking all night makes the bean soft...
ahzgly: The bean drank up water and got bigger and softer! Now rub the bean with your finger to peel off its skin.
qxm8tl: Wow, two halves! Tap the parts to learn their names. Try the magnifying glass too!
i2gmqf: Move the magnifying glass over the seed to look up close. Scientists use them to see tiny details!
y203u4: In the soil, the root grows down and the shoot grows up. This is called germination. The cotyledons feed the baby plant until its leaves can make food.
18gf6fv: You already found every part. Open the bean again to try the sprout!
5wtiau: You took a flower apart and helped a bee pollinate it!
15dduo5: Not yet! Take the flower apart and help the bee in Flower Lab.
19hj72v: Let's dissect a flower! Drag the pink petals and the green sepals off, one by one, into the trays. What's hiding inside?
hzkvqy: A bee buzzed in! Drag the bee to an anther to grab pollen, then to the sticky stigma.
m8lpei: Pull off all the petals first to see what's hiding inside!
1mmu6v0: The ovary grew into a fruit, and the ovules inside became seeds. Press Get a new flower to do it again!
jyb187: That's a stamen, the pollen maker! The fuzzy top is the anther, covered in yellow pollen. The thin stalk is the filament.
s9uka7: The pistil is in the very middle. Its sticky top, the stigma, catches pollen. The tube is the style. At the bottom, the ovary holds tiny ovules that can become seeds!
vz7aaa: The bee is dusted with pollen! Now drag it to the sticky stigma at the very top of the pistil.
3ypeq4: Pollen landed on the stigma! Watch: a tiny pollen tube grows down the style to the ovules...
1ixr7vq: Drag the bee onto one of the orange anthers first, to pick up pollen.
1l0pp1a: Those green leafy parts are sepals. They wrapped around the flower and protected it when it was a bud.
tybvh1: All 5 petals are off! Petals are bright and colorful to invite bees and butterflies. Now tap the parts in the middle.
f4ipu1: Nice pull! Keep going. Pull off every petal.
1pytr45: Pollen + ovule = seed! The ovary swelled up into a fruit with seeds inside. That's pollination. You're a flower detective!
702zql: Real flowers have the same parts. Next time you see one, look for the stamens and the pistil!
1kagpbp: You grew a bean plant through its whole life cycle!
18c9m7f: Not yet! Grow a bean all the way to new seeds in Grow a Bean.
efi79u: We planted a bean seed! To wake up, a seed needs water, air and warmth. Tap the watering can to give it a drink.
zeg8cu: Germination! The seed coat cracked and a tiny root poked out. Roots always grow down. Seeds don't need sunlight to sprout, just water, air and warmth.
1kuu0d3: Sprout! The shoot pushed up out of the soil. Those two round leaves are the cotyledons from inside the seed. Now it needs sunlight too!
18v4ibi: Seedling! The true leaves are opening. They catch sunlight and make food for the plant.
i1lgz2: Adult plant! It grew tall, with lots of leaves. Under the ground, the roots spread out to find water.
vnpk59: Flowers! The plant is blooming. Bees visit and carry pollen from flower to flower.
1xcpavy: Fruit and seeds! After pollination, the flowers turned into bean pods. Inside each pod are new seeds.
m64jdr: Glug glug! The water soaks into the soil and the seed starts to drink it up...
1s1wbax: Warm sunshine! The seed is still under the ground, so it only needs water and warmth for now.
1jidg4n: The pods dried up and popped open. The seeds fell to the ground and the life cycle can start all over again! Press Plant a new seed to grow another.
1flikej: The plant is thirsty! Its leaves are drooping. Tap the watering can.
11p6s0e: Clouds are blocking the sun. Plants need sunlight to make food. Tap the sun!
hq1jxn: You found 4 ways seeds travel to new places!
1vf0s4g: Not yet! Find all 4 ways seeds travel in Seed Travel.
1rz9s8q: Plants can't walk, so how do their seeds get to new places? Tap each picture to discover 4 ways seeds travel!
1bxgea: Four garden scenes: a dandelion in the wind, a rabbit near a burr plant, a coconut palm by the sea, and a popping seed pod. Tap each one.
17eyppj: Wind! Dandelion seeds have fluffy parachutes. A puff of wind carries them far, far away.
tu3wmt: Animal hitchhikers! Burrs have tiny hooks that grab onto fur. The animal carries the seed to a new place. People invented Velcro by copying burrs!
14lxa87: Water! Coconuts float. They can ride the ocean waves all the way to a new island and grow there.
eqw9vv: Pop! Some seed pods dry out and burst open, shooting their seeds away like tiny cannons.
9af8ii: One more way: birds and animals eat berries and fruits, then drop the seeds far away in their poop!
bzvuj0: Seeds inside! A tomato is a fruit. A fruit grows from a flower and holds the seeds.
1seurik: So many seeds! A cucumber is a fruit in disguise.
mjxsve: Seeds inside a zucchini too! It is a fruit, just like its cousin the cucumber.
1ocpcot: Look at all those seeds! A pepper is a fruit. The seeds grow on a little stalk in the middle.
1j5y9c1: Tricky one! A strawberry wears its seeds on the outside. Those tiny dots are seeds, so it is a fruit.
1dbx6ua: No seeds in celery. It is a stalk, the part that holds up the leaves. It is a vegetable.
